rationale: Every run is limited by an I/O-port path at ss/100C/1.60V. IO delays scale with the period (T_eff ~ 0.2*target + 3.6-4.4 ns), while reg-to-reg needs only ~4.2 ns, so keep period_frac 0.45. At 11.7 ns slack is +5 ns, so setup repair never runs. T_eff therefore tracks placement and wirelength, which are noisy (near-identical settings gave 5.95 vs 6.36). Hold, slew/cap (0, bar 0) and DRC are clean. Util 28 failed twice, so go back to the proven util 22. Keep timing-driven placement (clearly lowers port delay), routability off, DELAY 3, slew margin 35% (port buffering) and post-GRT timing/design repair for the tight re-runs. Leave density, margins, cap and RC free so the optimizer tries new placements near the best runs.
